english.title: Concerned in receipt / arrange to receive / removal / disposal of article for use in immigration crime
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse were concerned in the

(A)_[receipt of, or the arranging to receive, a relevant article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), from a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),]_
(B)_[removal or disposal of a relevant article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..) for the benefit of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),]_

knowing at the time of being so concerned that the article had been, was being or was to be used by yourself or another person in connection with an offence under section 24 or 25 of the Immigration Act 1971
english.legislation: Contrary to section 14(3), (4) and (8) of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 14(5) of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025 provides a defence of reasonable excuse.
(ii) This offence applies to conduct occurring both within and outside the United Kingdom (section 20).

other.penalty:
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
